episode_title: Episode 23: Brad Morrill and the acquisition of Richfield Trailer Supply

real_qa.q: How long did Brad Morrill's search and acquisition journey take from leaving Crystal Flash to closing on Richfield Trailer Supply?
real_qa.r: Brad left Crystal Flash on June 1, 2024, and closed on Richfield Trailer Supply exactly two years later on June 1, 2026. While the official search journey was 19 months from kickoff to close, the total journey including the five-month acquisition course and planning period was two years to the day.
real_qa.requete: Brad Morrill Richfield Trailer Supply acquisition timeline

real_qa.q: What was Brad Morrill's acquisition funnel from initial deal sourcing to closing Richfield Trailer Supply?
real_qa.r: Calder Capital brought 65 deals, while Brad sourced 20 independently for approximately 85 total in the top of funnel. He had initial conversations with 45-50 owners, conducted deep dives into 15 businesses, made five IOI/LOI offers, and ultimately closed on the fifth one, Richfield Trailer Supply.
real_qa.requete: acquisition funnel deals sourcing to close

real_qa.q: What was Brad Morrill's purchase price and down payment strategy for acquiring Richfield Trailer Supply?
real_qa.r: Brad had $500,000 to $600,000 of immediate personal cash available before considering family and friends or investors. Operating as a self-funded searcher with an SBA loan structure at 10% down, he targeted a $4 to $5 million valuation range, calculated from a $1 million EBITDA at approximately a four multiple.
real_qa.requete: SBA loan down payment self-funded acquisition size

real_qa.q: What geographic parameters did Brad Morrill set for sourcing Richfield Trailer Supply?
real_qa.r: Brad restricted his search to within an hour to 75 minutes of Grand Rapids, Michigan, which included the lakeshore, Muskegon, Holland, Kalamazoo, Battle Creek, Lansing, and the Grand Rapids area. As the search progressed, he adjusted these parameters and ultimately found Richfield Trailer Supply in Flint, Michigan, located 1 hour 45 minutes from his home.

real_qa.q: Why did Brad Morrill rule out manufacturing businesses during his search for Richfield Trailer Supply?
real_qa.r: Brad ruled out manufacturing because he lacked direct experience in manufacturing plants and wanted to focus on areas where he was already up to speed. He also noted that competitive pressure from others seeking manufacturing businesses was high. When he did visit a manufacturing prospect selling into automotive and appliance industries, the unknown variables and cyclical customer dynamics made the risk profile too high compared to distribution and service businesses.
real_qa.requete: why avoid manufacturing businesses acquisition search

guest.bio_context: Brad Morrill spent over 10 years in an executive role at Crystal Flash, an energy company with approximately 50-70 million dollars in revenue and 300 employees. He has extensive experience across multiple industries including the U.S. Army, Cargill (agriculture), Best Buy (retail), and self-employment as a solopreneur for five years while managing residential rental property for 18 years. He left Crystal Flash on June 1, 2024, to pursue business acquisition through a 19-month search process that concluded with the acquisition of Richfield Trailer Supply on June 1, 2026.
